description:
# AssurPrime — ENS Challenge Data #161 (Crédit Agricole Assurances)

Working data for **[Challenge Data #161, "AssurPrime : Saurez-vous prédire la prime d'assurance ?"](https://challengedata.ens.fr/challenges/161)**, proposed by **Crédit Agricole Assurances**, plus the intermediate artefacts needed to re-run a full two-stage pricing model.

The task: predict the **pure fire premium** on Pacifica's *Contrat Multirisque Agricole*, the multi-risk policy French farmers take out to cover their holding. Fire is the dominant share of that contract's claim burden. The target decomposes as

`CHARGE = FREQ x CM x ANNEE_ASSURANCE`

so the challenge asks for two models — one for **frequency** (`FREQ`), one for **average claim cost** (`CM`) — scored on RMSE against a GLM benchmark (Poisson/log for frequency, Tweedie/log for severity).

The approach these artefacts come from carves every qualitative feature with [AutoCarver](https://pypi.org/project/AutoCarver/) and tunes XGBoost with Optuna, weighting the severity model's samples by the frequency model's absolute error.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `train_input_Z61KlZo.csv` | Challenge training covariates, one row per policy-year, keyed on `ID`. Unmodified. |
| `train_output_DzPxaPY.csv` | Challenge training targets keyed on `ID`: `ANNEE_ASSURANCE`, `FREQ`, `CM`, `CHARGE`. Unmodified. |
| `test_input_5qJzHrr.csv` | Challenge out-of-sample covariates for submission. Unmodified. |
| `Incendies.csv` | Extract from the **BDIFF** national forest-fire database (IGN / Ministère de l'Agriculture), 24 columns. Joined during feature engineering to build the burnt-area and extinction-rate features (`total_surface_2023`, `total_surface_5y`, `surface_over_forest`, `fire_extinction_rates`). Not part of the challenge distribution. |
| `cm_carver_freq_tschuprowt_2026.json` | Serialized AutoCarver `BinaryCarver` (light mode), `CM` carved against the frequency target with Tschuprow's T. Used to stratify the train/dev split on the claim-amount distribution. |
| `frequency_2026.csv` | Frequency-model predictions on train + dev, keyed on `ID`; `pred_sum` is the expected claim count. Feeds the severity model's error weights. |
| `oos_frequency_2026.csv` | Same, on the out-of-sample test set. |

## Variables

- **Targets** — `FREQ` (claim frequency), `CM` (average claim cost), `CHARGE` (total cost).
  On rows with a claim, `CHARGE / CM` is exactly `FREQ * ANNEE_ASSURANCE`, an integer 1–5.
- **Exposure** — `ANNEE_ASSURANCE`, years since the contract was taken out.
- **Geography** — department plus weather/climate aggregates.
- **Contract** — insured's activity (cultivateur, polyculteur, ...), guarantee subscription
  flags, building count, employee count, claims declared at underwriting.
- **Surfaces / capitals / prevention** — building areas, insured capital by option, and
  protective equipment. The provider **anonymised these into `surface1..n`, `capital1..n`,
  `prev1..n`** for confidentiality; the names carry no meaning by design.

## Derived files

`frequency_2026.csv`, `oos_frequency_2026.csv` and `cm_carver_freq_tschuprowt_2026.json` are **not challenge originals** — they are produced by the frequency notebook and consumed by the severity notebook. Regenerate them whenever the frequency model changes; a stale pair describes a model that no longer exists.

## The 2025 winning solution

The saved 2025 models (AutoCarver 7.0.5 carvers, the XGBoost severity model and the frequency hand-off they consume) are published separately in [caa-challenge-2025-solution](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mariodefrance/caa-challenge-2025-solution). With this dataset and the repository's `tools/replay_2025_charge.py`, the 2025 baseline quoted in the article can be re-scored.
